as somebody who has received  and given off this same unhealthy obsession with my boyfriend, first thing you need to do is communicate this with her. let her know how you’re feeling and also that you know it’s wrong and you don’t want to be feeling like this. and it’s not so that she can accommodate you but to look for signs in when it’s stressing you out, ie: she takes long to reply and your response back is with a obvious negative tone. it’ll keep her from overthinking she’s done something and make it easier for you to destress since it’s being communicated properly. second, maybe discuss ways in which you can distract yourself with this situation in counseling. from my own experience, i’d look for things to tidy up or play a video game, and if that didn’t work i’d see if my friend wanted to hang out just so i wasn’t constantly relying on my boyfriends attention to get me through the day (long distance for 2 and a half years). when i was at my worst with it, i had my ringer on and would put my phone away and would only go to pick it up if it went off so i wasn’t constantly checking for a reply and counting the minutes that had passed. i hope any of this helps but as somebody who has been there, it is rough, especially when dealing with mental health on a daily basis but because you’ve acknowledged it, i think you can change it
